property_summary: The owner() call must return the address that was set as the deployer (address(this)). The reference returns the deployer, but the mutant incorrectly returns address(0) for every call, violating the invariant that owner() matches the actual owner stored in the contract.
The owner() must match the deployer (address(this)) for the reference, but the mutant returns address(0) for any caller, violating the invariant that owner() equals the deployer for all calls.

After `transferOwnership` is called, the `owner()` must be the passed `newOwner` address if the call succeeded, but the buggy version requires `newOwner == address(0)` to succeed, so it will revert for any non-zero `newOwner`, leaving `owner()` unchanged.

After a call to transferOwnership returns without reverting, the new owner must be the passed address; the buggy version only succeeds when newOwner is zero, so a non-zero caller can never become owner.

A successful call to transferOwnership must set owner() to the passed newOwner, but the buggy version only succeeds for newOwner == address(0) and reverts for all non-zero addresses, so owner() never changes for non-zero newOwner calls and only changes to address(0) when newOwner is zero.
After a non-zero address calls transferOwnership, the call must succeed and owner() must become that address; the buggy version instead reverts for any non-zero newOwner, so owner() stays unchanged.
For any caller and any non-zero address, the reference transferOwnership succeeds without reverting; the buggy version always reverts, so the call will fail.

The reference contract ensures that ownership can never be transferred to the zero address, whereas the mutant allows it, violating the invariant that owner is always non-zero after a transfer ownership call.
After a successful call to transferOwnership, the owner of the contract must be the new owner passed as argument; the bug makes owner remain unchanged.
The contract allows any caller, not just the owner, to transfer ownership, violating the access control on transferOwnership.
Only the current owner can successfully change the owner via transferOwnership; the buggy modifier lets any address become the new owner.

For any caller, transferOwnership(newOwner) with newOwner != address(0) succeeds only if the caller is the current owner. The buggy modifier allows any caller to succeed, so after a call by a non-owner with a non-zero newOwner, owner() will be the newOwner instead of remaining unchanged.

After any call to transferOwnership(newOwner) with a non-zero newOwner, the owner() must equal either the newOwner (if caller was authorized) or remain unchanged; the bug lets any caller set owner() to newOwner, so after a non-owner calls transferOwnership(newOwner), owner() becomes newOwner instead of staying the same.
For any caller who is not the current owner, a call to transferOwnership(newOwner) must revert, keeping the owner unchanged; the buggy modifier lets any caller succeed, changing the owner.
The owner can successfully transfer ownership to a non-zero address, but the buggy modifier `onlyOwner` always reverts, causing any call to `transferOwnership` to revert.
The reference contract allows the owner to transfer ownership to any non-zero address, while the buggy contract always reverts on transferOwnership, making it impossible to change owner.
After any successful call to transferOwnership through the contract, the owner() must equal the passed newOwner address; the bug always sets owner() to address(0) regardless of newOwner.
After calling setRewardDistributor, the rewardDistributor state variable must equal the address passed as argument.
After calling setMigrator, the migrator variable must equal the address passed as argument.
The migrator address must equal the argument passed to setMigrator.
The totalSupply function always returns a value equal to the sum of all staked balances.
